candidates.title: Check game-test CSV rows before importing

demandEvidence.chore: Record mobile game-test measurements, export them as CSV, and move the rows into a Google Sheet while avoiding missed or repeated files.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I test mobile games on a couple of phones and keep a simple log while I play: battery percentage, device temperature, frame drops, and a short note about what I was doing when it happened.

experimentPlan.output: A review table of supplied game-test CSV rows with missing fields and repeated keys flagged.
inputs: Synthetic device label and game session time
Synthetic battery, temperature, and frame-drop values
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a sample CSV export or fictional rows for review.
steps: Read supplied CSV rows without connecting to a phone or cloud drive.
Check required columns and flag missing values.
Compare operator-approved row keys and flag possible repeats.
Prepare a normalized table for a sample sheet.
Ask a person to verify flags and perform any import.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a labeled synthetic CSV, preserve expected measurements, flag planted repeated keys, and report missing fields without filling them in.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies fictional or authorized test data, chooses a safe duplicate key, and confirms flags and imports; the proposal does not control a phone or write to a live sheet.
unverified: Whether phone uploads can be reliably triggered is unsupported.
The CSV reference documents extraction into row objects, not upload monitoring.
The duplicate-removal reference documents comparisons, but correct keys for these logs are unknown.

ease.reason: The n8n CSV extraction reference (5c2bf4e7df8c3ec325ba2e74) documents turning CSV into row objects, and duplicate removal (f1662b0ceb942474f83a8108) supports comparison; neither covers phone uploads.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent game testers might pay for cleaner log imports; this post gives no purchase or payment evidence.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic CSV check is bounded; 5c2bf4e7df8c3ec325ba2e74 supports extraction and f1662b0ceb942474f83a8108 supports deduplication, while phone triggers remain unresolved.

autonomy.reason: The references 5c2bf4e7df8c3ec325ba2e74 and f1662b0ceb942474f83a8108 support row extraction and duplicate filtering; a person must choose keys, verify records, and import them.

evidence.reason: The retained spans describe measurements entered in a notes app, later CSV export and Sheet paste, plus a trigger firing zero or twice; this is one post.

candidates.reason: Concrete repeated logging and CSV transfer are described, and supplied n8n references support limited row extraction and duplicate checks. Provisional mean is 5.2, below 6; phone triggering and correct deduplication keys are unresolved.

candidates.title: Draft shipment delay notices from supplied rows

demandEvidence.chore: Notify a dispatcher when a shipment is delayed, based on an operator-supplied shipment status.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: A simple flow can notify a dispatcher when a shipment is delayed

experimentPlan.output: A draft dispatcher notice for a shipment row explicitly marked delayed.
inputs: Fictional current status and expected date
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies fictional shipment rows for a manual test run.
steps: Check that required status and date fields are present.
Apply a simple operator-defined delayed rule to each row.
Draft a notice for rows marked delayed.
Show the source row beside the draft.
Have a person verify status and send or discard the notice.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For labeled test rows, draft a notice only for rows marked delayed and show the matching input values without inventing shipment facts.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A dispatcher must define the delay rule, verify shipment facts, and approve any notice; no live logistics system or message delivery is part of this proposal.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference documents shipment system access or message delivery.
A real delay rule, required fields, and event timing are not specified in the retained spans.

ease.reason: A beginner can test a rule on fictional rows, but no supplied building reference supports the data connection or notification.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small logistics operators might pay for fewer missed delay updates; the post establishes no buying intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week offline mock can draft from test rows; shipment feeds, delay rules, and delivery remain unsupported.

autonomy.reason: The proposed loop can draft from supplied rows, but a dispatcher must verify status and approve messages; no integration capability is documented.

evidence.reason: The retained task span lists shipment-delay notices as an example, without a specific operator, frequency, fields, or corroboration.

candidates.reason: The retained task span gives a concrete notification chore that can be mocked with fictional rows. No supplied implementation reference supports live shipment access or message delivery; provisional mean is 4.4, below 6.

candidates.title: Turn rough sketches into reviewable wireframe drafts

demandEvidence.chore: Convert rough iPad sketches into higher-fidelity wireframes or illustrations.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I’ve been looking for a tool that can translate rough sketches on my iPad to higher fidelity wireframes or illustrations in near real time.

experimentPlan.output: A proposed wireframe draft from an operator-supplied synthetic sketch, with uncertain details marked for review.
experimentPlan.trigger: A designer supplies a fictional sketch and its intended screen purpose.
steps: Record the supplied sketch and constraints.
Create a draft layout matching only clearly identified elements.
Mark uncertain labels or relationships for review.
Compare the draft with the expected element checklist.
Have a designer revise and approve the result.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a small set of labeled synthetic sketches, the draft contains the expected named elements and marks ambiguous elements instead of silently guessing.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A designer must supply authorized imagery, clarify ambiguous intent, and approve all visual output; this proposal does not claim real-time iPad conversion.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference supports image-to-wireframe conversion.
Near-real-time behavior, visual fidelity, and tool availability are unverified.

ease.reason: The source describes a desired image conversion, but no supplied building reference supports image interpretation or wireframe generation.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent design professionals might pay to speed rough-sketch conversion; the post establishes no purchase intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic demo could be attempted, but image-to-layout generation and fidelity are unsupported by supplied implementation evidence.

autonomy.reason: Drafting may reduce some manual drawing, but a designer must interpret ambiguity and approve the output; no capability is documented.

evidence.reason: The fresh post states a specific desired conversion from iPad sketches to higher-fidelity wireframes or illustrations, but no frequency or corroboration.

candidates.reason: The request states a clear conversion task, so it receives an honest scoped assessment. No supplied implementation reference supports image conversion; provisional mean is 3.4, below 6.
